uncited: This method performs the forward pass of the C++/CUDA rasterizer for Time-of-Flight (ToF) Gaussian Splatting, extending standard 2D Gaussian Splatting to output phase and amplitude information alongside color and depth.

It solves the problem of rendering raw ToF sensor data (phase, amplitude) by treating phasors as additional vector attributes of the 3D Gaussians, allowing for differentiable rendering of depth and intensity maps.

It differs from its parent [2D Gaussian Splatting Rasterization](4815-2d-gaussian-splatting-rasterization.md) by explicitly handling complex-valued phasor accumulation and supporting phase/DC offset corrections, while differing from [Per-Primitive Texture Mapping for Reflective Gaussian Splatting](8629-per-primitive-texture-mapping-for-reflective-gaussian-splatt.md) by focusing on volumetric ToF signal synthesis rather than surface reflectance.
The method restructures arguments into a single tuple for the CUDA kernel.
**Argument Restructuring**: Construct the argument tuple as defined in the Data Structures section.
**Debug Handling**: If `raster_settings.debug` is true, deep-copy all arguments to CPU before invocation to preserve state for debugging.

Time and memory complexity are dominated by the CUDA rasterization kernel, which is $O(N \cdot P)$ where $N$ is the number of Gaussians and $P$ is the number of pixels, but optimized via binning and sorting.
The method supports differentiable rendering of ToF data, enabling joint optimization of geometry and ToF parameters.
Strengths include accurate simulation of ToF sensor noise and phase shifts.
Limitations include increased memory usage due to phasor attributes and potential precision issues with phase wrapping.
Originating from the "Gaussian Avatar Reconstruction" and "Gaussian Splatting" literature, this method extends 3D Gaussian Splatting to Time-of-Flight imaging.
It was introduced in the context of ToF Gaussian Rasterization (ToFGR) to enable differentiable rendering of depth and amplitude.
